$comment: What every key on the page is for. Sections describe where a group of strings appears; notes single out the ones that are constrained by something other than meaning. Read with GLOSSARY.md.

sections.meta: Never seen on the page. These are the search result, the browser tab and the card that appears when the address is pasted into a chat application. Written for someone who has not heard of Lukotta.
sections.ui: Controls in the header, and the link that lets a keyboard reader skip the navigation. Short, and read aloud by screen readers, so they must say what the control does rather than name it cleverly.
sections.nav: The header navigation. Each one matches a heading further down the page and should use the same words as that heading.
sections.hero: The first screen. One claim, one sentence explaining it, and the download button.
sections.trust: Four short assurances under the download button. Fragments, not sentences; no full stops.
sections.opens: The formats table — the heart of the page, and the reason most readers arrive. Terms are format names and stay as they are; the definitions are ordinary prose.
sections.how: Three steps, and the explanation of the Linux virtual machine underneath them.
sections.features: Six cards, one heading and one sentence each. What the application does once a drive is open.
sections.privacy: What is collected, which is nothing, and what the application asks the reader's Mac for.
sections.permissions: Three permissions macOS requires. The terms are Apple's own and must match what the reader sees in System Settings.
sections.requirements: What a Mac needs before the application will run. Four plain statements.
sections.faq: Eight questions, written as a reader would ask them. These are also published as structured data, so a search engine may show a question and its answer directly. Answers must stand on their own, without the question.
sections.footer: Links, the translation note, and the copyright line.

notes.meta.title: At or under 60 characters. Search results cut it off. Keyword first, brand last.
notes.meta.description: Between 70 and 165 characters. Longer is truncated mid-word.
notes.meta.ogTitle: The card title when the address is shared. May be shorter and less formal than meta.title.
notes.meta.imageAlt: Describes the Lukotta application icon, which is the shared card image.
notes.ui.skipToContent: The first thing a keyboard reader reaches. Must say plainly that it skips to the page content.
notes.hero.title: The one sentence the page is built around. Keep the full stop.
notes.hero.downloadNote: Contains {version}, which becomes the released version number. Keep the middle dots as separators.
notes.download.note: Same as hero.downloadNote, and should read identically.
notes.trust.1: Free as in the GPL, not free as in a trial. Where a language distinguishes these, use the word for the licence.
notes.trust.2: Two fragments joined by a comma.
notes.opens.drives.5.term: A category heading, not a product name. Translate the word for filesystems; leave ext4, btrfs and XFS as they are.
notes.opens.images.2.def: IMG and DMG are file extensions and stay in Latin script.
notes.opens.warning.title: A warning heading. Direct, not alarming.
notes.opens.warning.body: This is a safety statement about untested code. It must not be softened or made to sound more confident than the English.
notes.opens.specs: The whole string is a link to SPECS.md. It reads as a sentence, not as a button.
notes.how.1.body: Contains menu paths written with an arrow: File → Open Disk Image. Use the arrow, and Apple's own names for the File menu in this language.
notes.how.networkNote: Explains why the drive shows a network icon in Finder. Reassurance, so it must not sound like an apology or a defect.
notes.features.5.title: The number of languages. Update it here if the count changes.
notes.features.6.body: Bin is Apple's word for where a deleted application goes. Use whatever the reader's Mac calls it.
notes.privacy.body: A factual claim about what the application does and does not send. Do not strengthen it beyond the English.
notes.permissions.1.term: Full Disk Access, exactly as System Settings names it in this language.
notes.permissions.3.def: The claim that Lukotta never sees the administrator password is precise and load-bearing. Translate it exactly.
notes.faq.1.a: Names the GNU General Public License, which is not translated.
notes.faq.4.a: Explains the network icon again, for a reader who arrived at the questions first. It has to stand on its own.
notes.faq.6.a: Distinguishes writing to a real drive, which is safe, from writing to an image, which is untested. The distinction is the whole point of the answer and must survive.
notes.faq.7.a: A list of what cannot be opened, separated by commas and dashes. Keep it a single sentence if the language allows.
notes.footer.copyright: Contains {year} and {author}, both replaced when the page is built.
notes.footer.translationsBody: The invitation to report a bad translation. It appears above the list of every language.
notes.ui.switchToLight: The appearance button's spoken name while the page is dark. It names what clicking will do, not what the page currently is.
notes.ui.switchToDark: The same button while the page is light.
